On Saturday, the man was bitten just before 10:00 (02:00 GMT) at Horseshoe Reef - north-west of the popular Rottnest Island near the city of Perth, local police said. Aerial footage showed the man being rushed to shore by boat where paramedics and police performed CPR at the Geordie Bay jetty, local media ABC reported. "Sadly the man was unable to be revived," a police spokesperson said. The attack is the first fatal incident in Western Australia since March last year, when a surfer was mauled off a remote beach. Perth's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development told AFP news agency it received a report the man had been bitten by the great white shark.
The attack occurred at Horseshoe Reef - north-west of the popular Rottnest Island near the city of Perth, local police say.

Western Australia's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development told the AFP news agency it received a report that the man was bitten by the great white. Police later added: "About 9.55am on Saturday 16 May 2026, emergency services were advised of a possible shark attack off the coast of Rottnest Island.

It is the first fatal shark attack in Western Australia since March last year, when a surfer was mauled off a remote beach.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
A 38-year-old man has been killed by a 13ft (4m) shark in Western Australia.

On Saturday, the man was bitten just before 10:00 (02:00 GMT) at Horseshoe Reef - north-west of the popular Rottnest Island near the city of Perth, local police said.

Aerial footage showed the man being rushed to shore by boat where paramedics and police performed CPR at the Geordie Bay jetty, local media ABC reported.

"Sadly the man was unable to be revived," a police spokesperson said.

The attack is the first fatal incident in Western Australia since March last year, when a surfer was mauled off a remote beach.

Perth's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development told AFP news agency it received a report the man had been bitten by the great white shark.

The department urged the public to take "additional caution" in waters around the area.

Since records began in 1791, there have been almost 1,300 recorded shark attacks in Australia, with more than 260 of them resulting in death.

Earlier this year in January, four shark attacks were reported along the New South Wales coast over two days.

One of the victims included 12-year-old Nico Antic who jumped from a rock into the Sydney Harbour and was attacked by a suspected bull shark.

He died a week later, with his parents saying in a joint statement they were "heartbroken".

---

[Lähde: The Mirror]
A diver has been killed by a 13ft great white shark in a horror attack.

The 38-year-old man had been spearfishing with a friend when he was attacked at Horseshoe Reef, near Perth, Western Australia, police said. Aerial footage showed the man being rushed to shore after he was bitten with paramedics performing CPR on him.

A police spokesperson said: "Sadly the man was unable to be revived." Western Australia's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development told the AFP news agency it received a report that the man was bitten by the great white.

The department urged the public they should take "additional caution" in waters in the area. Police later added: "About 9.55am on Saturday 16 May 2026, emergency services were advised of a possible shark attack off the coast of Rottnest Island.

"A 38-year-old man was in the water at Horseshoe Reef when he was believed to have been bitten by a shark. The man was conveyed by vessel to shore, where he was met by SJA WA paramedics."

It comes after a large shark was seen about 87 yards offshore about the time of the attack, said Surf Life Saving WA. A report will be prepared for the Coroner, according to The Guardian.

Rottnest Island is a popular tourist destination in the Australian state. It is the first fatal attack in Western Australia since March last year. In that attack, a surfer was attacked on a remote beach.

There have been an estimated 1,300 shark attacks that have been recorded since 1791. Some 260 of those have since resulted in death.

[Lähde: International Business Times Singapore]
A 38-year-old man died Saturday after a suspected great white shark attacked him at Horseshoe Reef, one of Rottnest Island's most popular snorkeling sites off the coast of Western Australia.

Emergency services were called to Geordie Bay following reports of a shark attack in the water. Despite a rapid response involving helicopters, marine rescue crews, and paramedics, the man was pronounced dead after being brought ashore, according to Western Australia Police.

Authorities later confirmed the death would be investigated as a coronial matter.

Witnesses reported seeing a large shark in the area shortly before the attack. Media outlets, citing officials and eyewitness accounts, described the animal as a suspected great white shark measuring between 13 and 16 feet in length.

The Western Australia Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development issued a warning urging swimmers, snorkelers, and boaters to avoid the Geordie Bay area and exercise extreme caution.

Popular Tourist Area Known for Marine Life

Rottnest Island, located about 19 km (11 miles) off Perth, attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors annually for its beaches, reefs, and marine biodiversity.

Horseshoe Reef is particularly popular with snorkelers due to its shallow waters and clear visibility. However, marine experts note that baitfish activity in the area can also attract large predators, including sharks.

The incident has renewed attention on shark safety in Western Australia, which has recorded several fatal encounters in recent years. Since 1791, there have been almost 1,300 recorded shark attacks in Australia, with more than 260 of them resulting in death.

payload.title: Mies kuoli valkohain hyökkäyksessä Länsi-Australiassa
payload.summary: 38-vuotias mies kuoli lauantaina hain purtua häntä Horseshoe Reefin alueella Rottnest Islandin luoteispuolella lähellä Perthin kaupunkia. Viranomaisten mukaan kyseessä oli noin nelimetrinen valkohai.
payload.content:
38-vuotias mies on kuollut hain hyökkäyksessä Länsi-Australiassa lähellä Perthin kaupunkia. Poliisin mukaan mies joutui pureman kohteeksi lauantaina hieman ennen kello kymmentä aamulla paikallista aikaa Horseshoe Reefillä, joka sijaitsee suositun Rottnest Islandin luoteispuolella.

## Hyökkäys tapahtui Rottnest Islandin edustalla

Viranomaisille ilmoitettiin mahdollisesta haihyökkäyksestä noin kello 9.55 lauantaina 16. toukokuuta. Tapaus sattui Rottnest Islandin edustalla alueella, jota lähteissä kuvataan Perthin lähellä sijaitsevaksi suosituksi matkailukohteeksi. Horseshoe Reef mainitaan hyökkäyspaikkana useissa lähdekatkelmissa.

Yhdessä lähdetiedossa miehen kerrotaan olleen keihäskalastamassa ystävänsä kanssa, kun hyökkäys tapahtui. Poliisi ja alueen viranomaiset ovat vahvistaneet, että uhri oli 38-vuotias mies. Lähteissä tapausta kuvataan Länsi-Australian rannikolla sattuneeksi hyökkäykseksi.

## Elvytys ei pelastanut miestä

Paikallisten tietojen mukaan mies kuljetettiin pureman jälkeen veneellä rantaan Geordie Bayn laiturille. Siellä ensihoitajat ja poliisi yrittivät elvyttää häntä. Poliisin edustajan mukaan miestä ei kuitenkaan saatu virkoamaan.

Länsi-Australian alkutuotannosta ja aluekehityksestä vastaava viranomainen kertoi saaneensa ilmoituksen, jonka mukaan miestä puri noin nelimetrinen eli 13 jalan pituinen valkohai. Sama viranomainen kehotti yleisöä noudattamaan erityistä varovaisuutta alueen vesillä tapahtuman jälkeen.

## Ensimmäinen kuolemaan johtanut tapaus yli vuoteen

Tapaus on lähteiden mukaan Länsi-Australian ensimmäinen kuolemaan johtanut haihyökkäys sitten viime vuoden maaliskuun. Tuolloin surffaaja kuoli hain hyökättyä syrjäisellä rannalla.

Poliisin ja aluehallinnon julkiset tiedot keskittyvät tapahtumapaikkaan, ajankohtaan, uhrin ikään ja ilmoitukseen valkohaista. Lähteissä ei kerrota tarkemmin, mitä hyökkäystä edeltäneistä olosuhteista tiedetään tai onko alueella annettu muita rajoituksia varovaisuuskehotuksen lisäksi.
summary_bullets: 38-vuotias mies kuoli hain hyökkäyksessä Horseshoe Reefillä Länsi-Australiassa.
Viranomaisten mukaan ilmoituksessa mainittiin noin nelimetrinen valkohai.
Miestä yritettiin elvyttää Geordie Bayn laiturilla, mutta häntä ei saatu pelastettua.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu useiden lähdekatkelmien yhtäpitäviin tietoihin. Keihäskalastus mainitaan vain yhdessä lähteessä, joten se on esitetty varovaisesti lähdetietona eikä vahvana yleistettynä faktana.
